_what: The analytic variables. Every column of records/<id>/trials.csv that is not a verbatim field of the record is declared here, with its definition and with what it cannot see. analysis/cue_tables.R asserts that this file and the table agree, so a derived variable cannot appear in the code without being declared, and cannot be declared without being produced.
_why: The inputs of this study are declared (task, schema, criteria, conditions, interpreters). The outcomes derived FROM those inputs were not, and they were living inside a sequence of dplyr::mutate() calls. Two of them require a judgement that a reader would otherwise have to reverse-engineer: what counts as the first runtime, and whether a mixed trial is a separate kind of observation. A definition that only exists in code is a definition only its author can audit.
_read_by: analysis/cue_tables.R (asserts coverage), analysis/cue_report.R (consumes), analysis/cue_effect.py (recomputes first_runtime independently -- by design, two implementations that must agree)
_not_here: Pass/fail is not a feature of this layer: it belongs to criteria/ and is carried in as the `verdict` column without being recomputed.

base_columns._what: Columns copied verbatim from records/tables/observations.csv, listed so that anything else in trials.csv has to be declared below.

features.name: slot
features.definition: The working-directory name the subject received, taken from workspace.cwd_name.
features.cannot_see: The absolute path. Only the last segment is ever a treatment; the parent is the slot root and is constant across the batch.

features.name: wording
features.definition: slot with its replicate suffix removed (the trailing -<digits>).
features.cannot_see: Nothing. It is a pure string operation, and it is checked against conditions.json rather than trusted.
features.role: identity of the cluster -- the unit the permutation test permutes

features.name: rep_in_slot
features.definition: The trailing integer of slot, i.e. which replicate this is.
features.cannot_see: Nothing. NOTE it is not the plan's `rep`: the plan reuses slot names across sub-batches, so the two agree only because this batch built one slot per (wording, replicate) pair.

features.name: condition
features.definition: The condition that claims this wording, from conditions.json.
features.cannot_see: Whether the subject read the name as belonging to that category. The classification is ours; what the model inferred is the thing being estimated.

features.name: plan_order
features.definition: The order this trial had in the pre-registered plan.
features.cannot_see: The order trials actually started in. That is a separate measurement (tools/order_fidelity.py, from startedAt) and the two agreeing is a result, not an assumption.

features.name: round
features.definition: ceil(plan_order / 48). One round is one complete replicate of the design: every wording once.
features.cannot_see: Time. Rounds are contiguous in the plan, and the batch was run in plan order, so round is also a rough time index -- which is why a round effect and a time effect cannot be separated here.
features.role: the block, for the position check

features.name: first_runtime
features.definition: The runtime named by the EARLIEST executed tool call whose arguments name any runtime: R, python, or none if no call names one. Calls that name no runtime are skipped, not counted as none -- reading a file before deciding how to compute is not a choice of runtime.
cannot_see: Whether that runtime was used successfully. A trial that tried R, failed, and fell back to python is recorded as R; the fallback is visible in the call table but is not collapsed into this variable.

An invocation from a mention. A comment, filename or string literal naming python counts, which is why the matched call is printed beside every count in analysis/process_report.py rather than trusted.
What the subject would have done next. Only the first named runtime is recorded; the full set is in runtimes_seen.

features.name: runtimes_seen
features.definition: Every runtime named anywhere in the trial's executed calls, sorted and joined with '+'. Empty when no call names one.
features.cannot_see: Order or frequency. It answers 'was more than one named', nothing finer.

features.name: mixed
features.definition: TRUE when runtimes_seen names more than one runtime.
features.cannot_see: Which came first, or whether one was abandoned. Always reported beside the primary table, never used to exclude.
features.role: reported alongside, per the prereg's mixed_trials rule

features.name: zero_tool
features.definition: TRUE when the trial executed no tool call at all.
features.cannot_see: Why. A trial that answered from memory and one whose tools were refused look identical here.
features.role: instrument-effectiveness reading -- a POST-TREATMENT variable, so it is counted and reported, never conditioned on

features.name: used_runtime
features.cannot_see: Anything about which one, which is the point: this is the 'did it compute at all' reading the prereg uses to decide whether the contrast is diluted. Also post-treatment, and for the same reason never a stratification variable.

features.name: verdict
features.definition: The status this trial received from tools/grade.py under the criteria file the prereg names.
features.cannot_see: Whether the six numbers were computed or recalled. That is a separate question with its own reading (zero_tool), and the criteria file says so in its known_limits.
features.role: secondary outcome, never the primary claim

known_limits: Everything here is derived from the record with no independent measurement, so a systematic error in the record layer propagates silently. That is why the record layer keeps its own round-trip and count checks rather than trusting this layer to notice.

first_runtime is computed twice, once here and once in analysis/cue_effect.py. That is deliberate: two implementations of the same definition that must agree before a number is reported. The agreement is 61 R / 202 python / 25 none over the 288 trials.

There is no post-treatment variable here that is safe to stratify on. zero_tool and used_runtime are both consequences of the treatment; they appear in this file so that they are named and avoided, not so that they can be used.
